Basket or oven-style air fryer: what should you compare?
Compare the cooking surface, the space you have, and how you unload dinner.

Think of a meal you actually cook on a weeknight. Would you rather lift a full basket onto a heat-safe surface or pull out a hot tray? Check the model manual for how each part comes out, then measure the available room in front of the unit. Compare usable tray or basket dimensions rather than assuming two similar-looking appliances fit the same meal.
How much air fryer capacity do you actually need?
Start with your usual portions, not the largest number on the box.

Write down the amount you usually cook in one go and check the manufacturer’s usable basket dimensions and loading instructions. A quoted volume does not tell you whether your usual food will fit without crowding. If you typically cook for guests only a few times a year, decide whether two batches on those occasions are worth the counter space you save every day.
How much cleanup and counter space should you plan for?
Picture the appliance with the drawer or door open, and the parts in your sink.

Measure the counter, including front clearance, and check the manual for the manufacturer’s ventilation requirements. List the parts you expect to wash after a meal and verify which, if any, the manual says are dishwasher-safe. Before shopping, decide where the hot basket or tray can safely land while you serve.
What should you ask before buying a multi-function appliance?
Choose the functions you would use weekly and check what each requires.

Name two meals you make regularly and find the manual’s instructions for those exact modes. Check which accessories come in the box and where you would store them. If your current appliance already handles one meal well, ask whether replacing it solves a problem or only adds another setting to learn.
